passage:
Monday. Madhuri's phone rang eleven times before noon. A rough voice from a recovery office said, "Pay tonight, or we will call everyone in your contact list and tell them you're a cheat." The room seemed to tilt, and Madhuri almost transferred the money right then.

Wednesday. A colleague showed Madhuri a message from an unknown number that mentioned a debt. Shaking, Madhuri called Gurpreet, who said, "This is harassment, and it is not your fault. Don't pay in panic. Save every call log." They screenshotted the logs together.

Saturday. With Gurpreet beside Madhuri, a complaint went to the bank, then to the ombudsman's portal, and a copy of the screenshots went to the police. The calls did not stop at once, but that night Madhuri slept without the phone on the pillow.

qa.q: How many times did the phone ring before noon on Monday?
qa.a: The phone rang eleven times before noon on Monday.

qa.q: Why did Madhuri almost transfer the money on Monday?
qa.a: The threat to call everyone in the contact list and call Madhuri a cheat caused panic.

qa.q: What steps did Madhuri take to answer the harassment?
qa.a: Saved call logs and screenshots, complained to the bank, filed on the ombudsman's portal, gave the police a copy, and did not pay in panic.

qa.q: How did Gurpreet's words change the way Madhuri saw the situation?
qa.a: Gurpreet named it harassment and said it was not Madhuri's fault, so panic gave way to a plan.

grounding: Recovery agents threaten to call Madhuri's contacts; over several days Madhuri keeps records, does not pay in panic and reports the harassment properly.

passage:
Jana had missed two payments on a phone loan in Prague when the calls began. Then the messages: "We will contact your employer and your mother today if you do not pay." One agent read out her mother's phone number.
Her heart raced. She almost paid everything in her account right then, just to make it stop.
Her flatmate Diego saw her face. "That's harassment. They can't threaten you like that. Don't pay in a panic."
They sat at the kitchen table. Jana screenshotted every message and saved the call log. Diego looked up the consumer protection authority's complaint page. Jana wrote to the lender's official complaints address, attaching the evidence and saying she wanted to agree a repayment plan in writing. She also reported the threats to the police.
Then she called her mother herself. "If anyone calls you about a loan, just hang up. I'm handling it." Her mother said, "Okay. Are you all right?" Jana finally cried.

qa.q: What did the agent read out to Jana?
What was Jana feeling when the threats came?
qa.a: She felt panicked and frightened, her heart racing, almost paying everything just to make it stop.

qa.q: What did Jana do instead of paying under panic?
qa.a: She saved screenshots and call logs, complained in writing to the lender asking for a repayment plan, reported the threats to police and the consumer authority, and warned her mother.

qa.q: How might Jana's mother feel on hearing from her?
qa.a: Her mother may feel worried but reassured that Jana told her first and is handling it.

grounding: Recovery agents threaten to call the protagonist's family and employer; she recognises harassment, saves evidence, reports it and refuses to pay in panic.

passage:
At the logistics office in Pune, Gautam's desk phone rang. A man's voice, loud: "Your employee Gautam has not paid his loan. Tell him we'll visit the office." The receptionist transferred the call to HR.
Kavitha from HR called Gautam in. His face went white. He had missed two instalments on a personal loan after his father's surgery. The agents had already called his cousins.
"I'm so sorry, madam. I'm so ashamed."
Kavitha shook her head. "You don't need to apologise to me. Calling your workplace like this is harassment. It's not your fault."
She helped him make a plan: save every call log and message, write to the bank's grievance cell asking for a restructured schedule, and escalate to the banking ombudsman if needed. She also suggested he file a police complaint about the threats.
"And don't pay anyone who shows up here in cash," she added. "Anything goes through the bank."
Gautam nodded, his shoulders dropping for the first time that week.

qa.q: Why had Gautam missed two instalments?
What was Gautam feeling when Kavitha called him in?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and frightened, his face going white after the agent called his workplace.

qa.q: What plan did Kavitha help Gautam make?
qa.a: Saving call logs and messages, writing to the bank's grievance cell for a restructured schedule, escalating to the banking ombudsman if needed, and filing a police complaint.

qa.q: How might Kavitha see the agent's call to the office?
qa.a: Kavitha sees it as harassment, not a normal part of lending, and feels protective of Gautam.

grounding: Recovery agents threaten to contact the protagonist's workplace and relatives; an HR manager helps him see it is harassment, save evidence and report it.
